name: Japanese Pieris
description: Japanese Pieris (Pieris japonica), also called lily-of-the-valley shrub or andromeda, is a highly toxic ornamental shrub. It is related to azalea and rhododendron, which are also dangerous for cats. The plant contains grayanotoxins in the leaves, flowers, stems, and nectar. These toxins interfere with normal nerve and muscle signals. They can affect the digestive system, heart, and brain, even when a cat eats only a small amount. Signs may include drooling, vomiting, diarrhea, weakness, slow or irregular heartbeat, tremors, seizures, or collapse. This is an emergency exposure. Keep Japanese Pieris away from cats, and contact a veterinarian or emergency clinic immediately if your cat eats any part of it.
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: grayanotoxins I, II, and III (diterpenoid polyols); all parts toxic including nectar

Mechanism: grayanotoxins bind to voltage-gated sodium channels, keeping them open; this causes persistent depolarisation of cardiac and skeletal muscle, leading to hypotension, bradycardia, and arrhythmias
Symptoms: profuse drooling, vomiting, diarrhea, severe weakness, loss of coordination, abnormally slow heart rate, low blood pressure, tremors, seizures; can be fatal
Even small ingestions can cause serious cardiac effects in cats
Any suspected ingestion is a veterinary emergency requiring immediate care

symptoms.name: Vomiting, Diarrhea, Hypersalivation (Drooling), and Anorexia (Refusal to eat)
symptoms.notes: With small ingestions (a few leaves or petals), clinical signs are often limited to these gastrointestinal effects. The toxin can also cause abdominal pain.

symptoms.name: Cardiac Arrhythmias, Bradycardia (slow heart rate), Tachycardia (fast heart rate), and Hypotension (low blood pressure)
symptoms.notes: Grayanotoxins modify sodium channels in cardiac muscle cells, leading to prolonged depolarization. Hypotension may require intravenous fluid support.

symptoms.name: Weakness, Tremors, Seizures (Convulsions), Ataxia (loss of coordination), Depression, and Coma
symptoms.notes: The toxins affect nerve cells, causing prolonged excitation followed by depression. Severe CNS signs usually indicate a larger ingestion.

symptoms.name: Dyspnea (Difficulty breathing)
symptoms.notes: Trouble breathing is a common sign of significant grayanotoxin poisoning and often accompanies muscle weakness and cardiac issues.

symptoms.name: Transient Blindness / Blurred Vision
symptoms.notes: This is a specific, though less common, symptom associated with grayanotoxin ingestion (plants like Pieris and Rhododendron).
